known.title: A draft pull request can reach Ready while still behind a required base
A failed mergeability lookup can let green checks reach Ready

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. When a blocked review leaves the pull request as a draft and main advances on unrelated files, GitHub can report its documented `DRAFT` merge state. The trial merge is clean and this condition skips bringing main in. Close later marks the pull request ready after the check wait (`src/forge/close.py:395-402`) without reading its merge state again. On a repo that requires an up-to-date branch, it can therefore announce Ready while the owner cannot merge until close runs again.
findings.title: A draft pull request can reach Ready while still behind a required base

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. If `gh pr view` fails or returns unreadable JSON while the check API reports green, this code turns the lookup into `{}`. `_pending` then finds no reason to wait, so `_wait` returns success without learning whether GitHub reports a clash. This contradicts the existing check-wait contract at `src/forge/checks.py:6`, which treats a GitHub API error as not green yet, and can mark a conflicting pull request Ready during a transient lookup failure.
findings.title: A failed mergeability lookup can let green checks reach Ready
